correctness.rationale: Exact primitive identity and normalizations follow by differentiation and standard Laguerre orthogonality. \(F_n\) solves \(F_n''+F_n'+(n/x)F_n=0\), whence \(S_n'=(1-2x)(F_n')^2/n\) globally, yielding the two-root reduction and upper bound. Published compact-uniform Laguerre asymptotics for parameters zero and one yield \(n^{3/2}S_n(x)\to e^{-x}\sqrt{x}/\pi\); nearby oscillatory peaks give the matching lower bound. Envelope monotonicity localizes all maximizing roots. Stieltjes variation integration by parts and a single-jump extremizer show operator norm equality. Finite checker observations corroborate but do not replace this proof.

value.rationale: The precise variable-jump supremum is the intrinsic sharp norm of the nth Laguerre coefficient functional on the total-variation unit ball. Published fixed-jump coefficient rates and generic primitive methods do not evaluate the uniformly worst jump or its exact coefficient. A one-or-two-nearest-roots finite formula provides a computationally meaningful simplification; the half-line envelope gives a structural localization and closed leading constant.
